backwater_valves_7_4_6_4: (1) A backwater valve that would obstruct the free circulation of air shall not be installed on a building drain or building sewer, except as permitted by Sentence (2).
(2) A backwater valve may be installed on a building drain where it is of the normally open type, conforms to CAN/CSA-B70, B181.1, B181.2 or B182.1, and serves not more than one dwelling unit.

(3) Where a building drain or branch may be subject to backflow, either (a) a backwater valve shall be installed on the fixture drain of each fixture located below the level of the adjoining street, or (b) for a residential building served by a municipal sanitary sewer, a valve protecting fixtures located below the level of the cover of the upstream sanitary maintenance hole.
(4) Where several fixtures on the same floor are connected to the same branch, the valve may be installed on the branch instead of on each fixture drain.
(5) A subsoil drainage pipe discharging to a sanitary system subject to surcharge shall be connected so that sewage cannot back up into the pipe.
2024 change: the 2012 Code's 'gate valve or backwater valve' option in Sentence (3) is deleted - only a backwater valve; branch (3)(b) (maintenance-hole cover level) is new.
cleanout_locations_7_4_7_1: Cleanouts for both sanitary and storm systems, positioned to clean the entire system.
On the upstream side, directly above, every running trap.
Inside leader: at the base, or not more than 1 m upstream of the base (2024 value - the old/NPC figure is 3 m).
Building sewer NPS 8 or larger: the cleanout shall be a maintenance hole.

Building sewer between the building and the municipal sewer, and between cleanouts: no change of direction or grade (exception: pipe NPS 6 or smaller may change direction up to 5 degrees per 3 m, or by fittings totalling up to 45 degrees).
Building drain: a cleanout of NPS 4 or larger as close as possible to where the drain exits the building.
Stacks: at the base, within 3 m upstream of the base, or on the Y fitting connecting to the building drain or branch.
Indirect waste pipe serving food equipment: at every change of direction of more than 45 degrees.
Kitchen sink trap arm: a readily accessible cleanout as close as possible downstream of the trap.
cleanout_table_note: Table 7.4.7.2 is NEW in the 2024 OBC. Do not use the National Plumbing Code version: the NPC requires a same-size cleanout for NPS 3-4 drains; Ontario 2024 requires NPS 3.
maintenance_holes_7_4_7_2: Maintenance hole spacing: building sewer NPS 24 or smaller - not more than 90 m; larger than NPS 24 - not more than 150 m.
Developed length from the building to the first maintenance hole: not more than 75 m (2024 value - the 2012 Code said 30 m).
Sewer-to-sewer connection without a maintenance hole: developed length from the building to the connection not more than 30 m.
Sanitary building sewers NPS 8 and larger: maintenance holes at every junction and every change of slope, size or direction (storm sewers likewise).
One-way cleanouts must be arranged to clean in the direction of flow.
cleanout_access_7_4_7_4: Cleanout openings shall be readily accessible, shall not be located in a floor assembly where it would constitute a hazard, and shall not serve as a floor drain.
Every change of direction between a cleanout and the pipe it serves shall use 45-degree elbows.
Cleanout for a stack serving a wall-hung urinal: above the flood level rim of the fixture.
In contamination-risk occupancies (medical, laboratory): cleanouts serving fixture drains at least 150 mm above the flood level rim.
